meta.tier_interpretation_note: These tiers reflect salinity conditions (electrical conductivity, EC) at Emmaton (EM) and Jersey Point (JP) relative to low/moderate/high thresholds across months. Likelihood scores reflect policy-to-outcome plausibility—i.e., how strongly each legal standard can drive or constrain operations and flow/water-quality conditions affecting in-Delta salinity—not a guarantee of achieving any tier.

notes_on_metrics.ec_units: uS/cm (EC; agricultural salinity metrics commonly use EC normalized to 25°C)
notes_on_metrics.aggregation_rule: Uses the maximum of EM and JP for each month, then evaluates frequency of months below/above thresholds.

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan for the San Francisco Bay/Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta Estuary (Bay-Delta Plan)
Legal Standards.note: Establishes beneficial uses for in-Delta water (including agricultural supply and other uses) and sets water quality objectives (including salinity/EC objectives at in-Delta locations such as EM/JP, depending on the objective framework). Provides the main legal framework for managing freshwater conditions to limit salinity intrusion affecting in-Delta users.

key_elements.plain_definition: A recognized use of water (e.g., agricultural supply) that water-quality rules are designed to protect.
A numeric or narrative target (e.g., EC/salinity level) meant to protect a beneficial use.
Saltier ocean water moving inland into the Delta when freshwater flows are insufficient.
The amount of freshwater flowing from the Delta out to the Bay; higher outflow generally helps push salinity back seaward.

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641) implementing Bay-Delta Plan objectives for CVP/SWP operations
Legal Standards.note: Implements Bay-Delta Plan objectives through water right terms/conditions for CVP and SWP operations. D-1641 is a core operational compliance lever affecting salinity at in-Delta compliance locations (including stations like Emmaton and Jersey Point in many compliance frameworks).

key_elements.plain_definition: A monitoring point where EC/salinity is measured to determine whether objectives are being met.
A rule that changes pumping, reservoir releases, or flow patterns to meet a standard.
When measured EC/salinity goes above the allowed limit at a compliance location.

Legal Standards.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act (California Water Code §13000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: California’s foundational water quality statute giving the Water Boards authority to adopt water quality control plans (including the Bay-Delta Plan), set beneficial uses/objectives, and enforce requirements that protect in-Delta uses from high salinity.

key_elements.plain_definition: California’s State Water Resources Control Board plus nine Regional Boards that set and enforce water quality rules.
The set of actions and enforceable requirements used to meet objectives (often includes flow and operational controls).

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act (CWA) — water quality standards + Section 401 certification (33 U.S.C. §1251 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Federal law recognizing state water quality standards (beneficial uses + objectives) and requiring state certification for federally permitted/licensed activities that may discharge to waters. Can influence projects or actions affecting Delta hydrodynamics and salinity conditions relevant to EM/JP (often indirectly, project-by-project).

key_elements.plain_definition: The combination of beneficial uses and water quality objectives that must be protected.
The state must certify a federally permitted/licensed project will comply with water quality standards; the state can add enforceable conditions or deny.

Legal Standards.name: Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta Reform Act of 2009 (Water Code §85000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Creates the Delta Stewardship Council and the Delta Plan, embedding the ‘coequal goals’ (water supply reliability + ecosystem protection). It can shape large Delta decisions that affect salinity drivers (flows, conveyance, hydrodynamics), but typically operates as an indirect governance constraint rather than an EC standard at EM/JP.

key_elements.plain_definition: State goals to improve water supply reliability while also protecting, restoring, and enhancing the Delta ecosystem.
Certain covered actions must be consistent with Delta Plan policies.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Endangered Species Act (ESA) (16 U.S.C. §1531 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Not a salinity standard, but ESA can constrain CVP/SWP operations (exports, flow patterns, timing) to protect listed species. Those operational constraints can indirectly affect Delta outflow and salinity intrusion, influencing EC at in-Delta locations like EM/JP in some hydrologic/operational conditions.

key_elements.plain_definition: Federal agencies must consult to ensure actions don’t jeopardize listed species; resulting Biological Opinions can require operational changes.

Legal Standards.name: Central Valley Project Improvement Act (CVPIA) (1992) (Pub. L. 102-575, Title XXXIV)
Legal Standards.note: Requires fish-and-wildlife operational/restoration improvements tied to CVP operations. CVPIA-driven operational constraints can indirectly shift CVP export flexibility and flow management, which may affect salinity conditions experienced by in-Delta users.

key_elements.plain_definition: Water reserved/managed for environmental purposes, which can constrain export operations or change release patterns.

Legal Standards.name: California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) (Pub. Res. Code §21000 et seq.)
Legal Standards.note: Procedural law requiring disclosure of environmental impacts and feasible mitigation/alternatives for discretionary projects. CEQA can shape projects affecting Delta channels/hydrodynamics (barriers, conveyance changes, habitat projects) that may influence salinity at EM/JP, but it does not directly set EC performance standards.

key_elements.plain_definition: Measures to reduce significant environmental impacts of a project.
Evaluation of other ways to meet a project’s objectives with fewer environmental impacts.

Tier 1.threshold: Maximum of EM and JP is below the low threshold 75% of all months AND maximum of EM and JP is above the highest threshold no more than 5% of all months

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Direct framework for in-Delta salinity objectives aligned with Tier 1-like fresher conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Sets beneficial uses for in-Delta agriculture and other uses and adopts salinity/EC objectives with an implementation program that can require operational/flow conditions to limit salinity intrusion so EM/JP remain below the low threshold most months and rarely exceed the highest threshold.

policies.policy_name: D-1641 (implementation of objectives through CVP/SWP water right conditions)
policies.relationship: Direct operational compliance lever for managing salinity at in-Delta stations
policies.note: Mechanism: Translates plan objectives into enforceable operating terms for CVP/SWP; can constrain exports and require flow/outflow patterns that reduce high-EC months at EM/JP (subject to hydrologic feasibility).

policies.relationship: Foundational authority enabling Tier 1-relevant objectives, but indirect by itself
policies.note: Mechanism: Provides authority to set/enforce objectives; Tier 1 performance depends on the specific Bay-Delta objectives, implementation terms (e.g., D-1641), and enforcement posture.

policies.relationship: Conditional influence via standards recognition and project permitting/certification
policies.note: Mechanism: Anchors the water quality standards framework and allows §401 conditions/denials for federally permitted actions that might worsen salinity dynamics; influence is project-by-project rather than continuous operations control.

policies.relationship: Indirect—species-driven operational constraints may incidentally support fresher in-Delta conditions in some scenarios
policies.note: Mechanism: ESA constraints can reduce exports or alter timing/flows for species protection, which can sometimes increase outflow or reduce intrusion; effect on EM/JP is contingent on hydrology and the operational regime.

policies.relationship: Indirect—fish/wildlife operational requirements may reduce salinity stress in some conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Environmental allocations/operational requirements can constrain CVP flexibility and shift releases/exports, which may help keep EM/JP fresher in some months/years.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Governance influence; not an operational EC standard
policies.note: Mechanism: Can shape major Delta actions and long-term strategies affecting hydrodynamics/salinity drivers; effects on Tier 1 month-frequency targets are indirect and contingent.

policies.relationship: Procedural influence only
policies.note: Mechanism: Can require mitigation/alternatives for projects that worsen salinity intrusion, but does not provide direct operational control to reliably achieve Tier 1 frequency targets.

Tier 2.threshold: Maximum of EM and JP is below the low threshold at least 65% of all months, below the moderate threshold at least 75% of months, AND maximum of EM and JP is above the highest threshold no more than 12% of all months

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Direct objectives/implementation can plausibly support Tier 2 frequency-based salinity performance
policies.note: Mechanism: Through objectives protecting agricultural and other in-Delta uses, the plan can require flow/outflow/export constraints that keep EM/JP below low/moderate thresholds most months and limit high-threshold exceedances.

policies.relationship: Direct operational lever to manage frequency of higher-EC months
policies.note: Mechanism: Enforceable operating terms can reduce the frequency and duration of higher salinity at EM/JP by constraining exports and coordinating releases/outflow when required (subject to hydrologic constraints).

policies.relationship: Enabling authority; Tier 2 depends on specific plan objectives and enforcement
policies.note: Mechanism: Supports setting/enforcing objectives for in-Delta uses; actual Tier 2 outcomes depend on objective stringency and implementation choices.

policies.relationship: Conditional influence (project-by-project), not a primary operations lever
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 conditions can prevent worsening salinity drivers from specific federally permitted actions; not designed to continuously manage month-to-month EC at EM/JP.

policies.relationship: Indirect—may incidentally support Tier 2 in certain hydrologic/operational regimes
policies.note: Mechanism: Species protections can constrain exports and alter flows, sometimes reducing intrusion; influence varies by year and the specific operational constraints in place.

policies.relationship: Indirect operational influence
policies.note: Mechanism: Fish/wildlife operational requirements can shift CVP operations in ways that sometimes help reduce the share of high-EC months at EM/JP.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Indirect governance influence
policies.note: Mechanism: Shapes major covered actions that can influence salinity drivers; does not directly manage EC frequency targets.

policies.relationship: Procedural influence only
policies.note: Mechanism: Can require mitigation/alternatives for projects affecting Delta hydrodynamics, but cannot reliably deliver Tier 2 month-frequency performance on its own.

Tier 3.threshold: Maximum of EM and JP is below the low threshold at least 55% of all months, below the moderate threshold at least 65% of months, AND maximum of EM and JP is above the highest threshold no more than 20% of all months

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Primary legal route for tightening objectives/implementation if Tier 3 frequencies reflect poor protection of in-Delta uses
policies.note: Mechanism: If Tier 3 performance indicates frequent intrusion/high EC, Bay-Delta planning tools (objectives and implementation requirements) are the most direct legal lever to reduce the frequency of high-EC months at EM/JP (via flow/outflow/export constraints and coordinated operations where feasible).

policies.relationship: Direct compliance/enforcement and operational adjustment lever under stress
policies.note: Mechanism: Compliance monitoring and enforceable operating terms can trigger operational changes or highlight inability to meet objectives in extreme hydrology; D-1641 remains central to managing frequency of higher-EC months.

policies.relationship: Foundational authority to revise/enforce protections; indirect by itself
policies.note: Mechanism: Enables changes to objectives and stronger enforcement; real-world Tier 3 improvement depends on the specific revisions and implementation measures adopted.

policies.relationship: Conditional—can prevent additional degradation from specific federal permits/licenses
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 can condition/deny federally permitted actions that would worsen intrusion dynamics; does not directly manage ongoing operations driving monthly EC outcomes.

policies.relationship: Indirect operational constraint with contingent salinity benefits
policies.note: Mechanism: Export and flow constraints for species protection can sometimes reduce intrusion risk; however, Tier 3 frequency outcomes remain strongly hydrology-dependent.

policies.relationship: Indirect—may constrain exports/alter releases
policies.note: Mechanism: Environmental allocations/requirements can influence CVP operations affecting Delta flow patterns, with possible (not guaranteed) reductions in high-EC months at EM/JP.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Indirect governance influence
policies.note: Mechanism: Can affect major long-term actions and planning that influence salinity drivers; does not provide direct month-frequency salinity control.

policies.relationship: Procedural influence only
policies.note: Mechanism: Can require mitigation for projects that worsen Delta hydrodynamics; improvements to Tier 3 frequency metrics are contingent on project-specific outcomes.

Tier 4.threshold: Maximum of EM and JP is below the low threshold less than 55% of all months AND/OR maximum of EM and JP is above the highest threshold more than 20% of all months

policies.policy_name: Bay-Delta Plan (SWRCB Water Quality Control Plan)
policies.relationship: Tier 4 indicates poor protection of in-Delta uses; Bay-Delta objectives/implementation are the strongest direct legal levers for response
policies.note: Mechanism: Persistent high intrusion/high EC frequencies elevate the role of enforceable objectives and implementation requirements (flow/outflow/export constraints and coordinated operations) to improve in-Delta salinity conditions where feasible.

policies.relationship: Direct operational compliance/enforcement framework under extreme conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Central hook for operational adjustments and compliance accountability for CVP/SWP; Tier 4 conditions make D-1641 enforcement/terms especially consequential (while recognizing hydrologic limits).

policies.relationship: Foundational enforcement/planning authority; indirect by itself
policies.note: Mechanism: Authorizes stronger enforcement and plan revisions; actual Tier 4 improvements depend on the specific measures adopted (and available water/hydrology).

policies.relationship: Conditional—can restrict some worsening actions but not primary for ongoing EC outcomes
policies.note: Mechanism: §401 can prevent additional salinity-driver impacts from specific federally permitted actions; Tier 4 is usually dominated by hydrology and operations controlled through state planning and water-right terms.

policies.relationship: Indirect—may reduce exports/change flows with contingent salinity benefits
policies.note: Mechanism: Species protections can force export and flow changes that sometimes counter intrusion; Tier 4 outcomes can still occur in extreme drought/low inflow despite ESA constraints.

policies.relationship: Indirect—operational constraints may help but are not a salinity standard
policies.note: Mechanism: Fish/wildlife requirements can constrain CVP exports and influence releases; salinity improvements at EM/JP are plausible but not assured.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan consistency
policies.relationship: Indirect governance influence under chronic poor conditions
policies.note: Mechanism: Can influence long-term structural responses and covered actions; does not directly manage month-to-month EC exceedance rates.

policies.relationship: Procedural; project-specific influence only
policies.note: Mechanism: CEQA can reshape projects affecting hydrodynamics/salinity; it cannot directly compel operations to meet Tier 4 frequency thresholds.

Governing Agencies.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB)
Governing Agencies.note: Adopts/updates the Bay-Delta Plan; sets and enforces water quality objectives; issues/oversees water-right terms and the compliance framework for Bay-Delta objectives as implemented through decisions like D-1641.

Governing Agencies.name: Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCBs)
Governing Agencies.note: Implement Porter-Cologne regionally (Basin Plans, permits, enforcement) and coordinate with statewide objectives; roles intersect with projects affecting Delta tributaries and water quality drivers of salinity intrusion.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Water Resources (DWR)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the State Water Project; coordinates Delta operations (including exports and flow management) under applicable water quality requirements and biological constraints; actions can be shaped by Bay-Delta Plan/D-1641 requirements and project approvals under CEQA and Delta governance processes.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the Central Valley Project; coordinates with SWP and complies with applicable water quality requirements, ESA-driven operational constraints, and CVPIA-related operational/restoration requirements that can indirectly affect in-Delta salinity.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Governing Agencies.note: Federal oversight role for Clean Water Act programs including the water quality standards framework and certain regulatory authorities; not the day-to-day operator but central to CWA structure.

Governing Agencies.name: California Water Boards — CWA §401 Certification Program (SWRCB/RWQCBs)
Governing Agencies.note: Issues CWA §401 certifications and enforceable conditions/denials for federally permitted/licensed activities that may discharge to waters, including projects that could affect Delta salinity drivers (indirect, project-by-project).

Governing Agencies.name: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS)
Governing Agencies.note: Conducts ESA Section 7 consultations for listed anadromous fish affected by CVP/SWP operations; resulting BiOps can constrain exports/flows in ways that indirectly affect salinity intrusion risk at in-Delta locations like EM/JP (contingent on hydrology and operational regime).

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (USFWS)
Governing Agencies.note: Participates in ESA implementation for species under its jurisdiction and engages in CVPIA-related fish/wildlife efforts; can influence operational/restoration priorities that indirectly affect Delta flow patterns and salinity drivers.

Governing Agencies.name: Delta Stewardship Council (DSC)
Governing Agencies.note: Implements the Delta Reform Act’s governance framework via the Delta Plan and consistency process; influences major covered actions that can affect Delta ecosystem and water quality conditions over time (indirect effect on EM/JP salinity outcomes).

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW)
Governing Agencies.note: Often a CEQA trustee/responsible agency providing input on environmental impacts for projects affecting Delta habitat and hydrodynamics; can shape project design relevant to salinity management indirectly.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
Governing Agencies.note: Issues certain federal permits (e.g., dredge/fill) that may trigger CWA processes including §401 certification; can be involved in projects affecting channels/hydrodynamics relevant to salinity intrusion.
